title: Unity in Diversity
subtitle: One body, many parts — difference is the design.
objectives: Explain the one-body argument in 1 Corinthians 12
Explain why unity is not sameness
Name what holds a diverse group together

cards.title: Unity is not sameness
cards.text: The argument in 1 Corinthians 12 is anatomical. It says the opposite of what people expect: difference is the design.

cards.title: One body, many parts, different jobs
cards.text: The passage asks two questions and both are rhetorical.
points: **"If the whole body were an eye, where would the hearing be?"**
**A body of identical parts** is not a body.
**The eye cannot say to the hand, "I have no need of you."**
**Difference is not a problem to be fixed.**

cards.title: Tap a part
cards.text: Tap each one. The last button is the argument itself.

options: If all were an eye, where would the hearing be?
question.explain: A rhetorical question. A body of one part is not a body.

cards.title: Two opposite mistakes
cards.text: The passage names both, in order.
points: **Verse 15:** the foot says it is not a hand, so it does not belong.
**That is feeling useless.** The text denies it.
**Verse 21:** the eye says it has no need of the hand.
**That is feeling superior.** The text denies that too.

question.text: Verse 15 answers the person who feels…
question.explain: The foot saying it is not a hand does not make it less part of the body.

cards.title: What it does and does not say
cards.text: Read carefully, because it gets quoted loosely.
points: **It names real divisions:** Jew and Greek, slave and free.
**It says those divisions do not decide standing.**
**It does not say the differences vanished.**
**Equal standing, not erased identity.**

cards.title: A fan is four parts that cannot swap jobs
cards.text: Motor, capacitor, blade, switch — remove any one and nothing turns.
points: **The capacitor cannot do the blade's job.**
**The blade cannot start the motor.**
**No part is the important one.**
**Unity here means assembled**, not identical.

cards.title: A corner is four people with four jobs
cards.text: Nobody in a corner does what the fighter does, and the fight needs all of them.
points: **The trainer reads the fight.**
**The cutman works the swelling.**
**Somebody watches the clock and the water.**
**Four roles. One result.**

question.text: Unity in 1 Corinthians 12 means everyone being the same.
question.explain: Difference is the design. A body of identical parts is not a body.

cards.title: Many strands, one surface
cards.alt: A close view of handwoven rattan showing many separate strands crossing to make one surface
cards.text: Not one of them is the important strand. Pull any one out and it opens.

cards.title: A team of identical builds loses
cards.text: Any game with roles proves the passage accidentally.
points: **Five of the same class** cannot cover the map.
**The weakest-looking role** is often the one that holds it.
**Composition beats individual power.**
**That is the one-body argument** in a scoreboard.

cards.title: What to remember
points: One body, many parts, different jobs — difference is the design.
Verse 15 answers feeling useless; verse 21 answers feeling superior.
Galatians 3:28 removes the ranking, not the difference.
Unity means assembled, not identical.

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 7 Devotion. 1 Corinthians 12 is an anatomical argument, so the figure is anatomical: a single body with eye, ear, hand and foot tappable, each carrying its verse. The week is careful to give both halves of the passage, because it answers two opposite mistakes in order — verse 15 speaks to the person who feels useless and verse 21 to the person who feels superior, and quoting only one of them produces a lopsided lesson. Galatians 3:28 is read precisely: it removes the ranking rather than the difference. The fan teardown is the clearest version of the idea for this learner: four parts, no swapping, remove one and nothing turns.
discussion: Ask what the passage asks about an all-eye body.
Ask which verse speaks to feeling useless, and which to feeling superior.
Ask which part of a fan is the important one.
extension: Have him name four different roles in a group he belongs to and what each contributes.
Have him find 1 Corinthians 12:15 and 12:21 and read both.
misconceptions: "Unity means everyone the same." Difference is the design.
"Galatians 3:28 says differences disappeared." It says they do not decide standing.
"Some parts are more important." Verse 21 denies exactly that.
